title: Superflow vs Frame.io
kicker: · SUPERFLOW VS FRAME.IO · THE AI QA REVIEWER FOR AGENCIES
headline: Frame.io is a video review tool. Superflow is a QA tool + a team.
secondary: The team is AI agents, built from your QA checklist. They check every site change and pin what they find. Your team decides. Your client approves from a link.
prevents: Stop finding every mistake by hand.
No more manual pass before launch.
qualifier: If your agency ships client websites, not just video and creative post, this page is for you.
heroCaption: It's like Frame.io hired a QA team.

dimensions.label: Who checks the site
dimensions.framing: Frame.io's AI organizes the footage you upload. The live site never enters the picture.
leftFacts: Agents run your checklist. Every change, desktop and mobile.
Findings land as pinned comments, rationale attached.
rightFacts: A person leaves every comment on the footage.
AI (opt-in Frame.io Labs, experimental, plan-based usage limits) organizes projects, summarizes feedback across revisions, and powers search. It does not find issues.
dimensions.verdict: Frame.io's AI organizes what's already uploaded. Ours checks the live site itself, the part video review never touches.

dimensions.label: How the client says yes
dimensions.framing: Feedback is easy to collect. A yes is harder.
leftFacts: Multi-step review flows: agents check, your team gates, then the client.
Your client opens a link and taps Approve. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.
rightFacts: Share for Review links: reviewers need no account, entering name and email only on their first comment.
If approvals are enabled on the link, reviewers set each clip to Approved, In Progress, or Needs Review.
dimensions.verdict: Frame.io's review link is good and its per-clip approval statuses are real. The difference is the gate: in Superflow, the client's yes is one recorded step across the whole site.

dimensions.label: Where you review
dimensions.framing: Frame.io reviews the file. Superflow reviews the site it lives on.
leftFacts: Superflow lives on the site itself: passwords, Okta, SSO, no extension needed, guests included.
rightFacts: Frame.io reviews uploaded assets only: video, images, audio, PDFs, and 3D, in a cloud player with frame-accurate playback and a comparison viewer.
It does not load or check a running website at all.
dimensions.verdict: Different games, not a defect. Frame.io is built for finished and in-progress files. If your review is footage, Frame.io is the right tool for it.

dimensions.label: What stays private
dimensions.framing: Your team needs somewhere to disagree.
leftFacts: Internal-only notes your team sees and the client never does.
The debate stays private; the client sees one settled answer.
rightFacts: Internal comments separate client threads from team threads, gated to the Team plan and up ($25 per member per month).
dimensions.verdict: Both keep the argument away from the client. On Frame.io, team-only threads start on the Team plan, $25 per member per month.

dimensions.label: What gets captured
dimensions.framing: Both tools pin. The difference is what gets attached without asking.
leftFacts: Element and text pins, area comments.
A screenshot attaches to every comment automatically.
Recordings: screen, video, voice, from the toolbar.
rightFacts: Frame-accurate and range-based comments, annotations, version stacks, and a comparison viewer on every plan.
Auto transcription, speaker labels, and captions. Camera to Cloud uploads footage straight from the set.
No website screenshot or browser-session capture.
dimensions.verdict: Each captures its own medium well. Frame.io's frame-accurate tools are built for footage; Superflow's automatic screenshots and recordings are built for the live site.

dimensions.label: What it remembers
dimensions.framing: Boards hold tasks. They don't accumulate a client.
leftFacts: Brand rules and past decisions, learned once, fed to the agents next project.
rightFacts: No memory concept in product. Media intelligence indexes assets for search, but nothing persists learned context across projects.
dimensions.verdict: The tenth project should not start like the first.

dimensions.label: How it fits your stack
dimensions.framing: The fix still has to ship.
leftFacts: Two-way Asana, Monday, ClickUp. Slack built in.
rightFacts: Premiere, Final Cut Pro, Lightroom, and Camera to Cloud hardware, plus API, webhooks, Zapier, Make, and Adobe Workfront Fusion.
Approval status is settable and readable via the API. A packaged two-way sync to a named tool: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Frame.io's Adobe and NLE integrations run deep for creative work. We sync two-way with Asana, Monday, and ClickUp; no built-in Jira today.

pricingCompetitor: Verified July 2026: Free $0 (2 members, 2GB, 2 projects). Pro $15 per member/mo (5 members). Team $25 per member/mo (15 members, adds internal comments). Enterprise custom. Annual billing saves 13%. Reviewers are free and unlimited.
switchingLines: One snippet on any site; one click on Webflow, WordPress, or GTM.
Paste the checklist you already have; agents assemble from it.
Open Frame.io projects finish in Frame.io. Nothing migrates on day one.
honestCloseStrengths: Frame.io earned its place. Camera to Cloud gets footage from the set to the team before anyone leaves the shoot. Frame-accurate comments, version stacks, and a comparison viewer ship on every plan. Reviewers watch and comment free, no account needed. Its Premiere integration and NLE depth run deep.
stayLine: If your work is video and creative assets, and you want frame-accurate review, approvals, and footage straight from the camera, Frame.io is a strong fit. Stay.

faq.question: Is Superflow just Frame.io with AI added?
faq.answer: No. Frame.io's AI organizes and summarizes footage already uploaded. Superflow's agents check the live site itself, every change, and a person makes every call.

faq.question: Do the agents replace my reviewers?
faq.answer: No. Agents run the first pass. Your team, then your client, signs off.

faq.question: What happens to our Frame.io projects?
faq.answer: Finish them in Frame.io. Start new work in Superflow. Nothing migrates on day one.

faq.question: Will our clients have to learn a new tool?
faq.answer: No. They get a link and an Approve button. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.

faq.question: We also review video and creative assets in Frame.io.
faq.answer: Keep Frame.io for that. Superflow reviews the live site: pages, forms, and flows footage can't show.
